notes: §1985:XIV.3.2.3 SR2: "Cd-name-1 must reference an input-output CD when the I-O TERMINAL phrase is specified." communicationPath admits I-O only with TERMINAL, and BindPath maps it to a CdRule of formats [InputOutput], refusing through ResolveCommunicationCd (COBOL6170) a name that is no cd-name and an input or output CD. The witness refuses DISABLE I-O TERMINAL of an input CD. Probes at --std 85: (b) I-O TERMINAL of an output CD refused COBOL6170; of an input CD WITH KEY refused; of an undeclared name refused; of a containing program's I-O CD from a nested program refused; DISABLE I-O without TERMINAL refused COBOL5506. (d) DISABLE I-O TERMINAL CX WITH KEY "PW" accepted and ran, printing ST=21, then DISABLE OUTPUT CO printed ST=30. (c) the KEY phrase is refused at --std 2002 (COBOL0902), the facility at --std 2023. (a, e, f) not reached: the operand is a cd-name. Every refusal's text cites ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Annex A rather than the 1985 rule, the cross-cutting citation matter kb/Work PB4950 decides; the outcome is the one the rule requires.

next.reason: 1985: "Cd-name-1 must reference an input-output CD when the I-O TERMINAL phrase is specified."; 2023: "No DISABLE statement or communication description entries; no candidate covers the Communication module". The 2023 standard lacks the Communication module, its CDs and the DISABLE statement. The candidates are about unrelated file I-O rules and none covers this subject.
